From 12cab1191d9890097171156d06bfa8d31f1e39c8 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Deepakkumar Karn <dkarn@redhat.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Dec 2025 20:43:05 +0530
Subject: [PATCH] net: usb: rtl8150: fix memory leak on usb_submit_urb()
 failure

In async_set_registers(), when usb_submit_urb() fails, the allocated
  async_req structure and URB are not freed, causing a memory leak.

  The completion callback async_set_reg_cb() is responsible for freeing
  these allocations, but it is only called after the URB is successfully
  submitted and completes (successfully or with error). If submission
  fails, the callback never runs and the memory is leaked.

  Fix this by freeing both the URB and the request structure in the error
  path when usb_submit_urb() fails.

Reported-by: syzbot+8dd915c7cb0490fc8c52@syzkaller.appspotmail.com
Closes: https://syzkaller.appspot.com/bug?extid=8dd915c7cb0490fc8c52
Fixes: 4d12997a9bb3 ("drivers: net: usb: rtl8150: concurrent URB bugfix")
Signed-off-by: Deepakkumar Karn <dkarn@redhat.com>
Link: https://patch.msgid.link/20251216151304.59865-2-dkarn@redhat.com
Signed-off-by: Paolo Abeni <pabeni@redhat.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/usb/rtl8150.c b/drivers/net/usb/rtl8150.c
index 278e6cb6f4d9..e40b0669d9f4 100644
--- a/drivers/net/usb/rtl8150.c
+++ b/drivers/net/usb/rtl8150.c
@@ -211,6 +211,8 @@ static int async_set_registers(rtl8150_t *dev, u16 indx, u16 size, u16 reg)
 		if (res == -ENODEV)
 			netif_device_detach(dev->netdev);
 		dev_err(&dev->udev->dev, "%s failed with %d\n", __func__, res);
+		kfree(req);
+		usb_free_urb(async_urb);
 	}
 	return res;
 }
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Patch Modifications

### File: `drivers/net/usb/rtl8150.c`

**Modifications:**
- Added `kfree(req);` after the error handling block when `usb_submit_urb()` fails.
- Added `usb_free_urb(async_urb);` after the same error handling block.

These two lines are inserted inside the existing error branch (after the `dev_err()` call and before the closing brace) in the function `async_set_registers()`.

### Relationship Between Modifications

Both modifications address a single memory leak issue: when `usb_submit_urb()` fails, the previously allocated `async_req` structure (`req`) and the URB (`async_urb`) were not freed because the cleanup callback (`async_set_reg_cb()`) only runs upon successful submission. The two calls work together to release both allocations, ensuring no memory is leaked in the error path.
